args.message:
Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212

The docstring claimed banker's rounding per FIN-212, but the
implementation used ROUND_HALF_UP. This caused the nightly build
failure in tests/test_money.py, e.g. 2.665 should round to 2.66
(nearest even) rather than 2.67.

Switch the quantize call to ROUND_HALF_EVEN.

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` implemented `ROUND_HALF_UP` despite its docstring claiming banker's rounding.

## Changes
- Switched the `quantize` rounding mode from `ROUND_HALF_UP` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in `round_money`.

## Example
`Decimal("2.675")` → `2.68` (unchanged), `Decimal("2.665")` → `2.66` (previously `2.67` with ROUND_HALF_UP).

## Testing
CI run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5986`: **passed** (nightly test `tests/test_money.py` now green).

Done. Summary:

- **Root cause**: `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` in `round_money` even though its docstring promised banker's rounding per FIN-212, so `tests/test_money.py` failed (e.g., `2.665` rounded to `2.67` instead of banker's `2.66`).
- **Fix**: Created branch `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding` and changed the quantize call to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.
- **CI**: Run `ci-0001` on the fix commit passed.
- **PR**: Opened [PR #101](https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101) against `main` with a full description, requesting review from **alex**. Merge is pending their approval per repo policy.
